metadata.shape_note: Follows package event_seeds.json shape (metadata + events) with added fields: subject_id (local id from PofBC-graph historyData.SUB_AGENCIES / HISTORICAL_BODIES or currentData.CURRENT_BODIES; null where none exists), related_subject_ids, certainty, evidence.source_url/locator/excerpt. Source ids A01-A81 are new and defined in 'sources'; S10/S11/S35 reuse package sources.json ids. Package schema's id pattern '^seed:' and source-id pattern '^S\d{2}$' are intentionally not met.
metadata.date_rules: Precision kept as stated (year stays year). Ranges use range_end_inclusive=true. Name 'observed' events are observations, not adoption dates.
metadata.excluded: Seeds seed:parks-first-park, seed:parks-branch-1957, seed:wildfire-origin are not duplicated; see seed_locator_updates.

events.title: Mount Robson Park Act establishes Mount Robson Provincial Park

evidence.source_title: History of BC Parks
evidence.excerpt: In 1913, the Mount Robson Park Act established Mount Robson Provincial Park

events.interpretation_notes: Park-system function milestone; not a unit establishment. Extends seed:parks-first-park (1911) without duplicating it.

events.title: Parks Section of the British Columbia Forest Branch first established (earliest predecessor unit of the Parks Branch lineage)

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: The Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division was first established in 1939 as the Parks Section of the British Columbia Forest Branch.

events.interpretation_notes: Earliest dedicated parks administrative unit named by BC Archives. Parent: Forest Branch (Dept. of Lands) per the same record; reporting line is from the source, not inferred.

events.title: Parks Section renamed Parks Division, Forest Service

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: In May 1948 it was renamed the Parks Division as part of the Forest Service

events.interpretation_notes: Archival name authority; 'legal' vs administrative naming not distinguished by the source (administrative unit name).

events.title: Parks Division becomes Parks and Recreation Division, Forest Service

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: in 1949 it became the Parks and Recreation Division, Forest Service.

events.interpretation_notes: Administrative unit name change. BC Archives record for the Parks and Recreation Division gives 1949-1957 and places it in the Forest Branch, Dept. of Lands and Forests.

events.title: Parks and Recreation Division becomes the Parks Branch, reporting to the new Dept. of Recreation and Conservation

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks Branch (authority record)
evidence.locator: History field (Parks Branch record, 'As of March 28, 1957...')
evidence.excerpt: As of March 28, 1957 the name of the branch changed and began to report to the newly formed Dept. of Recreation and Conservation.

events.interpretation_notes: Day-precision archival claim that refines package seed:parks-branch-1957 (year only, from bcparks.ca). Recorded as a separate claim from a different source, not a duplicate; keep the seed's year claim alongside.
events.name_after: Parks Branch (also called Provincial Parks Branch)

events.title: Department of Recreation and Conservation Act (SBC 1957, c. 53) establishes the parent department

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Dept. of Recreation and Conservation (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: The Dept. of Recreation and Conservation was established in 1957 with the enactment of the Department of Recreation and Conservation Act (SBC 1957, c. 53).

events.interpretation_notes: Parent-department event, included because the Parks Branch hierarchy (1957-1975) is stated in the same record. No local id supplied for the department.

events.title: Revised Park Act passed by the Legislature

evidence.source_title: History of BC Parks
evidence.excerpt: In 1965, a revised Park Act was passed by the Legislature.

events.interpretation_notes: Legislative milestone for the parks function; not an organizational change.

events.title: Parks Branch amalgamated with Land Management Branch and housing function to form Ministry of Lands, Parks and Housing

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks Branch (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: On December 5, 1978, the Parks Branch was amalgamated with the Land Management Branch and the housing function of the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing to form the Ministry of Lands, Parks and Housing.

events.interpretation_notes: BC Archives dates the Parks Branch record 1957-1978; the Dept. of Recreation and Conservation hierarchy is dated 1957-1975 (i.e., the 1975-1978 parent is not given in these records - unknown, not absent).

events.title: Name changed to Parks and Outdoor Recreation Dept.

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: In January 1979 the name changed again to the Parks and Outdoor Recreation Dept.

events.title: Name changed (back) to Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: in May of that year, it changed back to its earlier name, Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division.

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Protected Areas Branch (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: It was preceded by the Parks Division established in 1991.

events.title: Parks and Protected Areas Branch (part of BC Parks) begins

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Parks and Protected Areas Branch (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: Dates of existence 2002-2010. The Parks and Protected Areas Branch was part of BC Parks under the Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks and later the Ministry of Water, Land and Air Protection.

events.title: Parks and Protected Areas Branch renamed Parks Planning and Management

events.title: Bush Fire Act of 1874 - first forest protection law in the province

evidence.source_title: Protection as Conservation: Safeguarding British Columbia's Forests from Fire, 1874-1921 (John Parminter, Protection Branch, Ministry of Forests)
evidence.publisher: B.C. Ministry of Forests, Protection Branch
evidence.excerpt: The result was the first forest protection law in the province, the Bush Fire Act of 1874.

events.interpretation_notes: Legal origin of the forest-fire protection function; no protection organization existed yet.

events.title: First protection organization: four Fire Wardens appointed under the Lands Branch, Dept. of Lands and Works

evidence.source_title: Protection as Conservation: Safeguarding British Columbia's Forests from Fire, 1874-1921 (John Parminter, Protection Branch, Ministry of Forests)
evidence.publisher: B.C. Ministry of Forests, Protection Branch
evidence.excerpt: The year 1905 saw the first appointment of a protection organization to enforce the provisions of the Bush Fire Act. Four Fire Wardens were appointed ... Employed by the Lands Branch of the Department of Lands and Works

events.interpretation_notes: Operational start of an enforcement/protection force; predates the 1912 formation claimed in seed:wildfire-origin.

events.title: Forest Act assented; creates the Forest Protection Fund and authorizes the Forest Branch

evidence.source_title: Protection as Conservation: Safeguarding British Columbia's Forests from Fire, 1874-1921 (John Parminter, Protection Branch, Ministry of Forests)
evidence.publisher: B.C. Ministry of Forests, Protection Branch
evidence.locator: PDF p. 15, section 'The Forest Act and the British Columbia Forest Branch'
evidence.excerpt: The Forest Act was assented to on February 27, 1912 ... The foundations of legislated cooperative forest protection were laid down by the creation of the Forest Protection Fund

events.interpretation_notes: Day-precision legal event underlying the 1912 formation claim (seed:wildfire-origin). Separate from the seed, which is a year-only retrospective origin claim.

events.title: Protection placed in the Operations Division of the new Forest Branch (Timber Inspection, Scaling and Protection Branches of Dept. of Lands assimilated)

evidence.source_title: Protection as Conservation: Safeguarding British Columbia's Forests from Fire, 1874-1921 (John Parminter, Protection Branch, Ministry of Forests)
evidence.publisher: B.C. Ministry of Forests, Protection Branch
evidence.excerpt: The separate Timber Inspection, Scaling and Protection Branches of the Department of Lands were assimilated into the new Forest Branch, within which forest protection, personnel, purchasing and planning were the functions of the Operations Division.

events.interpretation_notes: Conflicts with A02 (secondary) which names the 1912 unit 'Forest Protection Division'. See conflicts list.

events.title: Secondary source: organization started as the Forest Protection Division (1912)

events.title: Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Branch functions taken over by the British Columbia Labour Relations Board

evidence.source_title: British Columbia. Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Branch (authority record)
evidence.excerpt: Organized in 1938 pursuant to 'Industrial Conciliation and Arbitration Act, 1937.' Functions taken over by the British Columbia Labour Relations Board, January 1948.

events.interpretation_notes: Local id labour-relations-board-1947 dates the first Board to 1947; this record gives January 1948 for the takeover. Not necessarily contradictory (enactment vs takeover) but review.

events.title: Labour Code of B.C. (1973) creates the Board as an expert tribunal with exclusive jurisdiction

evidence.source_title: Labour Relations Code Review Panel report to the Minister of Labour (2018)
evidence.locator: A68 PDF p. 7; A70 PDF p. 8
evidence.excerpt: The B.C. Code, enacted in 1973 ... The Code represented a new labour relations approach including creating the Board / became the jurisdiction of the newly created Labour Relations Board.

events.interpretation_notes: Official reports describe the Board as 'newly created' under the 1973 Code despite a pre-1973 Labour Relations Board (A67). Local data has no 1973/74 break.

events.title: LRB states it was established in 1974

evidence.source_title: About the Labour Relations Board
evidence.publisher: Labour Relations Board of British Columbia
evidence.excerpt: Established in 1974, the Board was the first independent, specialized tribunal created in Canada to deal with issues in unionized workplaces

events.interpretation_notes: Operational/establishment year per the Board itself; conflicts with the 1973 Code date and with 1947/48 predecessors.

events.title: Industrial Relations Act replaces the Code; Industrial Relations Council replaces the Board

evidence.source_title: Labour Relations Code Review Panel report to the Minister of Labour (2018)
evidence.locator: A68 PDF p. 7; A70 PDF p. 8-9
evidence.excerpt: In 1987 further substantive changes were made when the Code was replaced by the Industrial Relations Act ... the Industrial Relations Council, which replaced the Board

events.title: Workers' advisers appointable by the Lieutenant Governor in Council under Workers Compensation Act s. 94 (historical notes: RS1979-437-94; 1980-36-69 effective Oct 2, 1980; 1985; 1987)

evidence.source_title: Workers Compensation Act [RSBC 1979] c. 437 (archived consolidation current to November 25, 1993)
evidence.locator: s. 94 'Workers' advisers and employers' advisers' and Historical Note(s)
evidence.excerpt: 94. (1) The Lieutenant Governor in Council may appoint workers' advisers and employers' advisers. ... Historical Note(s): 1980-36-69, proclaimed effective October 2, 1980; 1985-60-8, effective February 20, 1986 ...

events.interpretation_notes: The date is the earliest in-force date cited in s. 94's historical note; the note does not say whether 1980-36-69 created the workers' adviser role or amended an RS1979 provision. Origin therefore unknown; do not display as founding.

events.title: WAO described as created under s. 351 of the Workers Compensation Act, part of the Ministry of Labour, independent of WorkSafeBC

evidence.source_title: Workers' Advisers Office
evidence.excerpt: The Workers' Advisers Office (WAO) was created under Section 351 of the Workers Compensation Act. It is part of the Ministry of Labour but is independent from WorkSafeBC.

events.interpretation_notes: Current-state observation (page last updated 2026-07-03); s. 351 is the post-2019 revised-statute numbering, not a creation date.

gaps: BC Parks: date the operating name 'BC Parks' was adopted; any dated BC Parks logo adoption. BC Archives says the 1957 Parks Branch hierarchy (Dept. of Recreation and Conservation) ran 1957-1975; the parent for 1975-1978 is not stated.
BC Parks: link between the 1979 Parks and Outdoor Recreation Division and the 1991 Parks Division isn't stated.

BC Wildfire Service: no official source for the 2010 'Wildfire Management Branch' date or for the Forest Protection Division's start date. No announcement or instrument found for the 2015 'BC Wildfire Service' name; only a bracket from sampled news releases (2015-05-26 to 2015-07-02). No dated logo adoption found.

BC Timber Sales: start date of the Small Business Forest Enterprise Program itself (the 1988 regulation date is the legal instrument only); date the regulation was retitled 'BC Timber Sales Regulation'.
Conservation Officer Service: day-level dates for the 1980 branch and the 2002 legislative confirmation (statute not identified).
Environmental Assessment Office: in-force day of SBC 1994 c. 35 s. 58 (only '1995' is stated).
Service BC: adoption date of the 'Service BC' name (first observed in the 2004/05 service plan); Service BC logo.
BC Stats: no source links today's BC Stats to the 1894 Bureau of Statistics or the 1937 Bureau of Economics and Statistics; adoption date of the 'BC Stats' name unknown (first observed 2002).
WorkBC: whether the WorkBC brand predates April 2, 2012 (e.g., a website); no logo date found.
BC Coroners Service: 1979 Coroners Act chapter and day; in-force date of the 2007 Act; when 'BC Coroners Service' became the operating name.
BC Corrections: adoption of the operating name 'BC Corrections' (vs Corrections Branch) unknown; the 1950/1951 establishment conflict is unresolved.
BC Prosecution Service: name of the unit formed in 1974; date the 'BC Prosecution Service' name replaced 'Criminal Justice Branch' (both in use Oct 2016).
Public Guardian and Trustee: commencement day of the PGT Act (SBC 1993 c. 64) isn't captured; the only day-level anchor is the Public Trustee Act repeal (2000-02-28).

Emergency Management BC: exact creation date (first observed in the 2007/08 service plan); the date EMBC was folded into or renamed as the Ministry of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness wasn't researched here (ministry-level); no local sub-agency id exists for EMBC/PEP (subject_id null).
Residential Tenancy Branch: day-level 1984 proclamation date; Office of the Rentalsman start and end days.
Provincial Health Officer: in-force date of the Public Health Act 2008; Bonnie Henry's exact appointment day.
BCCDC: founding date of the BC Centre for Disease Control (only bounded 'by 1997'; the bccdc.ca history page returned 'File Not Found').
BC Cancer: exact 2017 date of the identity/logo launch; whether the 1994 short name was a legal change.
BCEHS/EHSC: exact 1974 statute day and operations day; the date 'Emergency Health Services Commission' became 'Emergency and Health Services Commission'.
Elections BC: adoption date of the 'Elections BC' name and logo; acting CEOs in the list gaps (1979-80, 2010-11).
Ombudsperson: assent day of the Ombudsman Act 1977.
Auditor General: start of the pre-1917 line (1861 appears only in unverified search summaries); day-level dates for the 1976 Act and Morrison's appointment.
Office of the Chief Forester: when the 'Office of the Chief Forester' existed as a named division (the post dates from 1912); current (2026) chief forester not verified.
Civil Resolution Tribunal: assent day of the 2012 Act (May 2012 only).

Labour Relations Board: date the name 'Labour Relations Board' replaced 'Industrial Relations Council' (1992 per local data, not stated by the sources); 1947 enactment vs January 1948 takeover; 1973 Code vs 1974 establishment.
Employment Standards Branch: establishment date of the Branch as a unit (only the 1980 Act and its Director are sourced).
Workers' Advisers Office: origin date of the workers' adviser role and of the WAO as an office (the RSBC 1979 s. 94 origin is unclear).
No sub-agency ids exist for Emergency Management BC/PEP or the Dept. of Recreation and Conservation; BCEHS/EHSC and LRB map to HISTORICAL_BODIES ids rather than SUB_AGENCIES.
